open_problems.open_problem: Complete a checked proof that the corrected rho_n is the sharp weak-overlap frontier for the repaired public-function ATE experiment across absolute risk, root-MSE, fixed-probability risk, and honest interval length.

source_refs.excerpt: both minimax absolute risk and minimax root mean-squared risk are equivalent to rho_n.
the discharged core supports only a parametric lower floor plus estimator-side achievability
the class-uniform U_n≍R_n comparison and R_n^* upper frontier are not discharged

source_refs.claim: The paper proves structure-agnostic optimality of doubly robust ATE estimators when nuisance information is supplied only through black-box estimation rates, furnishing the regular benchmark that the repaired weak-overlap experiment changes.
source_refs.author: Jikai Jin and Vasilis Syrgkanis

source_refs.claim: The paper derives minimax ATE lower bounds and matching estimators in structure-agnostic nuisance classes with optional smoothness, but does not supply the corrected one-sided weak-overlap shell frontier.
source_refs.author: Matteo Bonvini, Edward H. Kennedy, Oliver Dukes, and Sivaraman Balakrishnan

source_refs.claim: The paper proves thresholded cross-fitted AIPW Wald validity under weak-overlap tail and nuisance conditions, but studies sufficient inference conditions rather than this matched global-L2 minimax risk.
source_refs.author: Jacob Dorn

open_problems.why_unsolved: The failed v1 frontier combined an overly large treated-regression stochastic penalty with law-specific shell constants and lacked a shell-matching converse, so it established only an upper envelope and a root-n floor. The authoritative repair replaces the penalty by r1/sqrt(n lambda), imposes uniform dyadic shells, and supplies four least-favourable channels. The adjacent literature establishes structure-agnostic regular-overlap benchmarks or sufficient weak-overlap Wald conditions, not this exact matched risk. A checked resolution still has to verify uniform class membership, the fuzzy-mixture collision/KL bound, cap-binding cases, the maximum-to-sum reduction, and the median-of-five risk and interval upgrades.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A verified minimax characterization with risk equivalent to Q_kappa(n,r1)+r1 n^(-kappa/[2(kappa+1)])+r1 re^(kappa/(kappa+2))+r0 re, plus a fixed-probability converse and an honest interval with expected length of that order.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation and problem formulation center global ATE optimality on black-box prediction-error guarantees, which is exactly the repaired experiment's starting point.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: ATE estimation uses learned nuisance functions -> global prediction accuracy defines a structure-agnostic benchmark -> one-sided weak overlap creates four additional obstructions -> characterize their sharp combined frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Structure-agnostic paired experiments and lower-bound channels for doubly robust ATE estimation under supplied nuisance rates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The repaired result keeps the same public-function experiment but must localize the hard alternatives into dyadic weak-overlap shells.

method_exemplars.technique: Localized fuzzy-hypothesis lower bounds with calibrated regression perturbations and target separation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The nuisance-product converse likewise needs a mixture whose sample laws stay close while the causal target concentrates at separated values.

method_exemplars.technique: Thresholded cross-fitted AIPW score analysis with overlap-tail and nuisance-rate bookkeeping.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The attainable side uses the same clipped-score architecture, but must prove sharp risk and bias-aware interval guarantees rather than only a Wald limit.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct an ATE estimator adaptive to an unknown overlap exponent and unknown nuisance radii that attains the oracle corrected rho_n frontier, and determine the unavoidable adaptation penalty.

source_refs.excerpt: Explicitly leave adaptation to unknown tail/radii, interval calibration
an adaptive clipped or thresholded ATE estimator that is minimax-rate optimal

open_problems.why_unsolved: The attainable clipping scale is the maximum of b_o=n^(-1/(kappa+1)), b_e=re^(2/(kappa+2)), and, when active, b_g=(n r1^2)^(-1), so the corrected estimator presumes the tail exponent and nuisance certificates. A data-driven rule must compare tail bias, no-treated-observation bias, nuisance-product bias, and inverse-weight fluctuation without using the unknown quantities. The first proof step that changes is the deterministic oracle threshold: it must be replaced by a Lepski, aggregation, or self-normalized selector with a uniform oracle inequality.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An adaptive clipped or aggregated doubly robust estimator with a uniform oracle inequality over ranges of kappa,r0,r1,re, together with a lower bound deciding whether exact adaptation or a logarithmically inflated rho_n is unavoidable.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates thresholding from weak-overlap instability while insisting that bias correction preserve the original causal target.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Weak overlap destabilizes doubly robust estimation -> thresholding controls small denominators -> bias correction preserves the population ATE -> unknown tail and nuisance difficulty require a data-driven minimax threshold

method_exemplars.technique: Threshold-indexed robust IPW inference with uniform control of small-denominator behavior.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An oracle selector must compare the same family of thresholded estimators while controlling fluctuations uniformly over thresholds.

method_exemplars.technique: Bias-corrected trimmed doubly robust estimation that retains the original treatment-effect target.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The adaptive procedure must stabilize inverse weights without silently changing the full-population ATE.

method_exemplars.technique: Tail-aware thresholded AIPW analysis with explicit nuisance-rate bookkeeping.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its indexed weak-overlap controls are the natural starting point for a simultaneous oracle inequality over candidate clip levels.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the sharp weak-overlap ATE minimax frontier for every admissible pair of uniform shell constants, including classes too restrictive for the repaired note's reservoir construction.

source_refs.excerpt: For matching lower bounds assume positive treated-noise allowance and a class rich enough
arbitrarily restrictive shell constants outside the theorem.
the proof yields law-specific comparison constants, not a class-uniform U_n asymp R_n statement

open_problems.why_unsolved: The repaired upper bound works with fixed uniform shell constants, but the matching lower-bound reservoirs require explicit inequalities on c_- and c_+ so that untouched and perturbable tail mass both fit in the class. For tighter nonempty shell classes, the current R=0,1,2 allocation may be impossible. The first proof step that changes is construction of the common baseline shell law and untouched reservoir: it must be redesigned for arbitrary admissible constants or shown impossible, with any loss of target diameter quantified.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient characterization of admissible shell-constant pairs and a matched minimax risk for each regime, either preserving rho_n via a new least-favourable family or giving the modified frontier when class geometry suppresses an obstruction.

writing_exemplar.why: Its support-condition narrative is the closest template for explaining how quantitative tail geometry controls irregular treatment-effect rates.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Inverse weighting is irregular without quantitative support control -> shell constants determine how much hard tail mass is available -> restrictive geometry may exclude standard least-favourable experiments -> index the rate by feasible shell geometry

method_exemplars.technique: Localized fuzzy-hypothesis construction with explicit mass and amplitude calibration.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The shell-constant question is exactly whether localized masses and amplitudes can be recalibrated while keeping product divergence bounded.

method_exemplars.technique: Sharp structure-agnostic lower bounds built from explicit hard subexperiments sharing public nuisance approximations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A resolution must characterize which hard subexperiments remain embeddable in the restricted shell class and what target diameter they retain.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether the corrected rho_n frontier remains sharp when potential outcomes or individual treatment effects are uniformly bounded, replacing the Gaussian treated-noise least-favourable families.

source_refs.excerpt: leave adaptation to unknown tail/radii, interval calibration, bounded-treatment-effect variants
Generate Y(1)=g1(X)+sigma Z, Y(0)=g0(X) with conditionally independent Gaussian treated noise

open_problems.why_unsolved: The repaired lower bounds use positive Gaussian treated noise and signed tail perturbations, which yield smooth KL calculations and the Q_kappa noise channel but violate bounded-potential-outcome restrictions. The first proof step that changes is the outcome channel: it must be replaced by a bounded Bernoulli, Rademacher, or compact-support experiment while retaining common public functions, the cancellation identity, the global L2 certificates, bounded product divergence, and the same target separation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A matched minimax theorem over a uniformly bounded-potential-outcome or bounded-treatment-effect class with the same rho_n rate, or a counterexample and replacement rate identifying exactly which lower-bound component changes.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames limited-overlap ATE inference through an explicit restricted outcome-response class and asks what optimal estimation remains possible.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Weak overlap makes unrestricted ATE recovery unstable -> restrictions on outcome responses can restore control -> bounded responses alter the available least-favourable channel -> characterize the sharp restricted-class frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Bounded localized regression perturbations embedded in fuzzy-hypothesis lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired converse needs bounded response perturbations that preserve class membership while producing a causal-target separation.

method_exemplars.technique: Upper and lower structure-agnostic ATE comparisons under explicit nuisance approximation classes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its regular benchmark is the natural comparator for deciding whether weak-tail localization alone changes the bounded-signal rate.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the maximal nuisance-rate region in which clipped cross-fitted AIPW yields uniformly valid studentized inference under very weak overlap, and prove necessity outside that region.

source_refs.claim: The paper gives sufficient black-box conditions for clipped AIPW and explicitly identifies its propensity-rate bound as potentially lax, leaving whether it can be weakened open.
source_refs.author: Jacob Dorn

source_refs.claim: The paper derives Gaussian and non-Gaussian IPW regimes indexed by propensity tails and trimming, but not a sharp necessity frontier for two estimated AIPW nuisances.
source_refs.author: Xinwei Ma and Jingshen Wang
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Dorn controls the clipped-score remainder using black-box nuisance bounds and a propensity-tail integral, but identifies the propensity-rate restriction as possibly proof-driven. Existing IPW tail-regime results do not decide whether violating it creates a genuine statistical obstruction or merely defeats the current small-propensity decomposition. Resolving necessity requires least-favourable estimated-nuisance sequences or counterexamples aligned with the studentized statistic, not just a sharper sufficient remainder bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient phase diagram in the overlap-tail index, outcome-regression error, propensity error, and clipping threshold for uniform studentized asymptotic normality, including explicit counterexamples outside the valid region.

writing_exemplar.why: It poses the black-box feasibility question, supplies a clean sufficient region, and isolates the remaining propensity-rate sharpness issue.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Weak overlap breaks ordinary AIPW remainder control -> clipping restores Gaussian inference under stated nuisance rates -> one propensity restriction may be proof-driven -> locate the exact validity frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Cross-fit the clipped AIPW score, split by propensity magnitude, and compare remainder bias with the diverging oracle standard deviation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired phase diagram sharpens the same remainder decomposition rather than changing the estimator or estimand.

method_exemplars.technique: Neyman-orthogonal score expansion with sample splitting, product-of-nuisance remainder control, and uniform Gaussian approximation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the bounded-overlap product-rate benchmark that must be localized and renormalized in the weak-overlap model.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a feasible bias-aware confidence interval for the full-population ATE with uniform coverage and rho_n-order expected length when overlap-tail constants and nuisance-error radii are unknown.

source_refs.excerpt: For fixed alpha and supplied radii/class constants, construct an honest confidence interval
These are bias-aware intervals, not a claim of Gaussian/Wald validity.

source_refs.claim: The paper ties conventional ATE coverage error to small local comparison samples under limited overlap and develops a small-sample correction under classical local-normal structure.
source_refs.author: Christoph Rothe

source_refs.claim: The paper gives finite-sample optimal bias-aware ATE intervals under normal known-variance errors, while feasible unknown-error versions are asymptotic.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong and Michal Kolesár

source_refs.claim: The paper obtains uniform asymptotic Wald validity for thresholded AIPW under weak overlap but reports moderate finite-sample overrejection and does not calibrate the corrected minimax bias radius.
source_refs.author: Jacob Dorn

open_problems.why_unsolved: The authoritative interval uses supplied radii and class constants to turn a uniform probability bound into a deterministic bias radius around a median-of-five estimator. The literature's finite-sample remedies instead rely on normality, known variance, or local smoothness, while modern clipped-AIPW Wald results are asymptotic and may overreject at moderate effective sample sizes. The missing step is an observable upper confidence bound for tail mass and nuisance approximation error that preserves uniform coverage without treating the non-Gaussian or bias-dominated regimes as regular Wald problems.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computable confidence interval with uniform 1-alpha coverage and expected length of order rho_n over the repaired class with unknown calibration constants, or an adaptation lower bound proving the minimal necessary inflation.

writing_exemplar.why: It makes coverage distortion from limited local comparison samples, rather than estimator variance alone, the motivating problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Weak overlap creates tiny effective comparison samples -> conventional coverage is governed by those local counts rather than total n -> oracle bias-aware radii need unknown class constants -> build feasible honest intervals with near-optimal length

method_exemplars.technique: Bias-aware critical values from a conditional minimax-linear problem, calibrating interval length to worst-case bias and conditional variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the nearest honest-length benchmark for the same ATE when overlap is too weak for ordinary root-n inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Cross-fitted clipped AIPW with empirical score variance and threshold calibration under weak-overlap tails.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the modern feasible score construction whose Wald calibration must be replaced or augmented by the repaired bias-aware radius.

method_exemplars.technique: Bias correction for propensity trimming that retains the original ATE.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its observable bias accounting is structurally analogous to the calibration needed without changing the estimand.

literature_map:
1. Khan and Tamer (2010, Econometrica, 10.3982/ECTA7372) establish the identification-versus-estimability tension: inverse weights can force irregular, tail-dependent rates.
2. Crump, Hotz, Imbens, and Mitnik (2009, Biometrika, 10.1093/biomet/asn055) optimize precision by trimming to a new overlap population, making the estimand-change tradeoff explicit.
3. Rothe (2017, Econometrica, 10.3982/ECTA13141) ties distorted ATE coverage to local weak-overlap sample sizes and develops a small-sample-oriented interval.
4. Yang and Ding (2018, Biometrika, 10.1093/biomet/asy008) smooth estimated-propensity trimming so design-stage uncertainty enters inference, while still targeting a trimmed population.
5. Li, Morgan, and Zaslavsky (2018, JASA, arXiv:1609.07494) use bounded overlap weights that improve precision but change the target away from the population ATE.
6. Ma and Wang (2020, JASA, arXiv:1810.11397) show Gaussian and non-Gaussian IPW regimes indexed by propensity tails and trimming and propose robust adaptive inference.
7. Hong, Leung, and Li (2020, Econometrics Journal, 10.1093/ectj/utz017) let propensities drift with n and derive an effective-sample rate based on the smallest treatment probability.
8. Heiler and Kazak (2021, Journal of Econometrics, 10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.03.025) obtain stable limits and an adaptive m-out-of-n bootstrap under irregular overlap.
9. Armstrong and Kolesár (2021, Econometrica, arXiv:1712.04594) give finite-sample optimal bias-aware ATE inference under outcome smoothness and normal known-variance errors.
10. Sasaki and Ura (2022, Econometric Theory, arXiv:1709.00981) estimate and remove trimming bias for ratio moments using boundary smoothness.
11. Jin and Syrgkanis (2024, arXiv:2402.14264) prove structure-agnostic optimality of doubly robust ATE estimators under black-box nuisance rates.
12. Bonvini, Kennedy, Dukes, and Balakrishnan (2024, arXiv:2405.08525) derive structure-agnostic ATE minimax bounds with added smoothness and matching estimators.
13. Ma, Sant'Anna, Sasaki, and Ura (2023, arXiv:2304.08974) preserve double robustness after propensity trimming through joint bias correction.
14. Dorn (2025, arXiv:2504.13273) gives uniform Wald validity for clipped cross-fitted AIPW and explicitly leaves a propensity-rate sharpness issue.
15. Together these papers cover trimming, irregular limits, structure-agnostic optimality, and sufficient weak-overlap inference, but not the operator-supplied four-channel rho_n frontier or feasible calibration with unknown shell and nuisance constants.
